The respondent hasn't reached a conclusion and is still gathering information on costs and feasibility. This could be a good agenda topic: bringing in manufacturers or 3PLs who have already made this decision to share their ROI analysis frameworks.

themes.deepDive: This is a single but specific example that speaks to a broader question many manufacturers face: whether to outsource logistics or bring it in-house. IRG's approach of spinning off a fleet as its own profit center offers a potential case study for the committee on vertical integration in freight. With only one respondent citing this, more input is needed to see if this model is seen as replicable or unique to IRG's scale and industry. The respondent's framing suggests this could be a strong panelist topic: turning transportation from cost center to revenue driver.
details: IRG Transport is a food processing company that created its own trucking fleet.
The fleet operates as a separate, self-sustaining business that complements the parent company.
This model directly addresses how manufacturers can make transportation profitable rather than just a cost center.
themes.summary: One respondent points to IRG Transport as a leader for spinning off a self-sustaining fleet from its core manufacturing business.
